notes.claim: A vector is a quantity with a magnitude (length) and a direction, such as velocity, force or acceleration.
Two vectors with the same magnitude and direction are equal wherever they sit, so an arrow can be moved without changing the vector.
Moving backwards along a vector makes it negative, which means reversing its direction.

sources.title: Vectors: FAQ (article) | Vectors | Khan Academy
sources.quote: A vector is a mathematical object that has both a magnitude (length) and a direction. Vectors can be used to represent physical quantities such as velocity, force, and acceleration.

sources.title: Geometric vectors - Geometric vectors - Higher Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: If two vectors have the same magnitude and direction , then they are equal regardless of their position.

sources.title: Subtracting vectors - Using vector components - National 5 Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Subtracting a vector is the same as adding a negative version of the vector (remember that making a vector negative means reversing its direction).

sources.title: Geometric vectors - Geometric vectors - Higher Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: If we move 'backwards' along a vector, it becomes negative
